iddialar.alinti: Infrared photographs revealed a pentimento where the blessing hand's thumb is more upright.

iddialar.alinti: A woodworm-infested marouflage panel was on the back of the painting. When specialist Monica Griesbach removed it, the painting broke into seven pieces.

iddialar.alinti: The pigments and the walnut panel upon which the work was executed are consistent with other Leonardo paintings.

iddialar.iddia: Yüzdeki sfumato etkisi, görünüşe göre kısmen boyanın avuç kenarıyla işlenmesiyle elde edilmiştir ve Leonardo'nun birçok eserinde tipiktir.
iddialar.alinti: The sfumato effect of the face—evidently achieved in part by manipulating the paint using the heel of the hand—is typical of many works by Leonardo.

iddialar.alinti: Sir Francis Cook, 4th Baronet, Cook's great-grandson, sold it at auction in 1958 for £45 (equivalent to £900 in 2025) as a work by Leonardo's pupil Giovanni Antonio Boltraffio, to whom the painting remained attributed until 2011.

iddialar.alinti: London's National Gallery authenticated Salvator Mundi as an autograph work by Leonardo and exhibited it from November 2011 to February 2012.
